limits.statement: createSupportExplanation keeps a capability whose status is supported and whose evidenceRefs list is empty. The rule that a supported entry names its provenance exists for fields (fixture explanation-rejects-supported-field-without-provenance: a supported field without provenance is refused) but not for capabilities, so a supported label in an explanation is not evidence that anything was checked.

projectFiveStateCapabilities refuses a supported record that has no evidence and one whose evidence is a plain string. It accepts a supported record whose artifact ref is a hand-built object of the right shape (a repeated-character digest): the ref is shape-checked and no artifact is looked up. Through the legacy adapter boolean bridge (source legacy-adapter-boolean) a supported record with no evidence at all is accepted and carries only a constraint that names its source.

buildSupportEvidenceMatrix keeps a supported cell that cites no evidence, and supportEvidenceMatrixDiagnostics reports nothing for it. Diagnostics exist for partial and unknown cells only (fixture matrix-diagnostics-for-partial-and-unknown), and an unknown or partial explanation of the same capability takes precedence over a supported one (fixtures matrix-unknown-beats-supported and matrix-partial-beats-supported). A supported cell summarises what an explanation said; it is not a checked claim.

validateAdapterSdkManifest refuses a network or subprocess allowance, an inherited loader variable such as NODE_OPTIONS, an environment assignment and an absolute read root. It accepts a manifest that requests a write root and one whose environment list names credential-like and system variables (a secret access key, a token, PATH, HOME). A valid manifest is therefore not a statement that its permission request is acceptable; the validator is a shape check, and activation stays non-executable and needs manual approval.

The manifest names a verification basis from a fixed vocabulary and has no field that ties a basis to a recorded run: a manifest that declares production-repo validates with nothing behind the claim. The fixture package declares synthetic-only, and runtime-tested is refused as a basis (fixture manifest-rejects-runtime-tested-basis). What a declared basis rests on is not recorded.

validateSdkResponse refuses a response with a top-level capabilities key and one whose status is supported, but accepts a result object that claims support for a capability nobody declared (a made-up capability name and a supported flag): the result is bounded data and the validator does not interpret it.

validateAdapterTaskPacket refuses an empty write scope, a short base sha and an uppercase one. It accepts a write scope that names everything, a root path and a path outside the repository, and it accepts a base sha made only of zero characters: the sha is shape-checked and no commit is looked up.

reviewAdapterPackage compares the inventory with the manifest and, when the caller passes an observed package digest, with that digest (a different digest is reported, fixture package-review-reports-wrong-digest). It does not read the package, as its own note says (fixture package-review-with-matching-digest): an inventory whose file digest, size and package digest belong to no real file passes when the observed digest equals the one in the inventory, and an inventory that lists a file the manifest does not mention passes. packageBytesTrusted is false also when the digests match, and no comparison is made (digestMatch null) when no observed digest is passed.

reviewAdapterSubmission reaches ready-for-execution-review with preExecutionReviewPassed true while executable stays false. A failing conformance report passed with the other arguments does not change the review (compare observed-gap-submission-review-ignores-conformance with submission-review-of-fixture-package), and a package whose only capability is unknown reaches the same status with an unknown diagnostic. Without explanations or with a support conflict the review is not ready (fixtures submission-review-without-explanations and submission-review-support-conflict). Ready is a structural readiness status: it is not an approval to execute and not a support claim.

For a bskel range whose lower bound is above its upper bound, a duplicate read root, a response for another request id, a duplicate inventory path and an inventory whose declared sizes add up past the aggregate limit, the JSON Schema file accepts the document and the runtime validator refuses it (schemaAccepts true, runtimeAccepts false, agree false in each gap fixture). A consumer that validates with the schema files alone accepts more than the runtime does. The fixture schema-parity-both-reject-network-allow is a manifest that both refuse.

The schema length limits count characters while the runtime limits are in UTF-8 bytes: a title or a snapshot reference of three-byte characters that is within the character limit and over the byte limit is accepted by the schema and refused by the runtime. A control character in the adapter title and a Windows device name as an inventory path are also accepted by the schema and refused by the runtime (schemaAccepts true, runtimeAccepts false, agree false in each gap fixture).

A textual search of the test files of the track for the name of each export (the exportUsage builtin) finds the onboarding journey test naming the conformance harness, the package inventory, the SARIF conversion and the task packet, but neither reviewAdapterSubmission nor buildSupportEvidenceMatrix. A name in a file is not an exercise, so the search is coarse; what the journey does not cover is not recorded.

package.json at the base commit holds the text sdk in no letter case: its files allowlist lists directories such as bin/ and lib/ but not the SDK directory, and none of its scripts names the SDK tests. By this allowlist the SDK is not part of the published package. An install of a packed tarball followed by an import of the SDK is not recorded here (audit item T22-05).

No file in the directories and files that package.json lists under files mentions sdk/next or sdk-next at the base commit, so no shipped file, bin/ included, imports or names the SDK directory (a path built at run time would not be seen by this search). The one shipped file that names the SDK manifest contract is lib/trust-next/external-adapter-permissions.mjs (the anchor); it holds the contract string as its own constant and does not import the SDK, so the two copies of the string are not tied to each other by an import.

The files listed under references, outside sdk/next and test/sdk-next, contain the text sdk/next at the base commit (recomputed with git grep): the documents of the scale-sdk folder, the T00 ownership files and the nested runner. They describe, route to or own the SDK; none of them is in the shipped scope of the previous limit.

No file outside sdk/next and test/sdk-next has an import, from or require line that names sdk/next at the base commit (git grep; the anchor is the mention search of the previous limit, run over the same scope). By this search nothing consumes the SDK; an import with a computed path would not match.

The root test script is node --test test/*.test.mjs, which matches test files directly under test/ and not test/sdk-next. The suite runs through node scripts/run-next-nested-tests.mjs T22 (the CI step T22 sdk-next of the nested-next job) or through node --test on its test files (the direct-tap command). The files listed under references hold the root script and the CI step; a green root npm test is not T22 evidence.

The documents listed under references state a pass figure for the SDK suite measured on a worktree, not on the pinned commit, on Node 18, 22 and 24. They are not pinned or compared by this record and are not edited by it. The figures that count here are the ones the commands level recomputes from the pinned commit; the CI jobs recorded in ci_observations ran Node 22 and Node 24, and no run on Node 18 is recorded.

limits.statement: The conformance harness calls an invoke function that the caller supplies in the same process (a module path is refused), and the activation plan of the fixture package is not executable (executable false, approval required). The only worker exercised is the fixture worker of the minimal package, whose verification basis is synthetic-only. No real third-party adapter, no worker process and no enforcement of the declared permissions was observed. Observing one needs an adapter package from a real source and the permission layer of the trust track that decides activation; neither is part of this record.

The SDK sources import no npm package. The schema-parity fixtures load ajv from the node_modules of the checkout that runs them. The commands run in an extracted copy of the base commit whose node_modules is linked to the node_modules of that checkout. Before the link is made, the version of every package named in environment.loaded_packages is compared with the version that package-lock.json states at the base commit, and a difference fails the test. The files inside the installed packages are not hashed.

Only the minimal fixture package and hand-built manifests, requests, explanations, inventories and constants are recorded (a repeated-character digest stands in for a real one). Behaviour on real adapters or packages, any performance, scale or concurrency figure, and behaviour under other locales or time zones (the commands run with LC_ALL=C and TZ=UTC) are not recorded.

The recorded outputs, hashes and counts were generated on one machine (see environment) with one Node major. Other operating systems, architectures and Node versions were not observed by this record; the test replays the fixtures on whatever Node runs it and reports a difference.

Whether the SDK contracts (the manifest, the worker protocol, the descriptor and the schema files) are stable, and how a change of one of them would be promoted or rolled back, is not recorded: this record is provisional and pins what the code does at the base commit (audit item T22-06).

verification.recomputed: bytes, git_blob_sha1 and sha256 of every pinned file, per-file and total test counts, the exit code and counts of both commands, the first runner line, every fixture output hash and every expected value, the reference lists and the absence checks of the limits that carry them, the installed version of every package in environment.loaded_packages against package-lock.json at the base commit, and the per-file table, every test count, the NESTED_SUITE line and the base commit that the README states are compared by baseline-record.test.mjs with the values it recomputed, never with a copy kept in the document.
levels: always: the record is well formed, and any single tampered hash, size, test count, exit code, expected value, limit status or commit id is reported; artifact_digest covers every field except its own value, so an edit of a limit statement, a fixture class, a call, a title or this text that is not re-sealed is reported

live files: size, sha256 and blob id are recomputed from the checkout; a file that disagrees in one hash or in size alone is damage and fails; a file that matches neither hash is drift, which skips the live replays while the pinned commit decides

pinned commit: the base commit is fetched once when absent and the sizes and digests of all pinned files, the runner included, are recomputed from its own blobs; if the commit is unavailable the test fails, and only BASELINE_ALLOW_UNVERIFIED=1 turns that into an explicit skip
ancestry: a shallow checkout is deepened with git fetch --no-tags --unshallow origin and the base commit must be an ancestor of HEAD

commands: both recorded commands are re-run in an extracted copy of the base commit (node_modules linked from the checkout once the installed versions equal environment.loaded_packages, which package-lock.json at the base commit states) and must reproduce exit code, counts, per-file counts and every fixture output; the fixtures call the pinned SDK modules and the pinned fixture adapter package, and the two builtins of the record library (schemaParity, which compares a schema file with the runtime validator through ajv, and exportUsage, which lists the pinned test files that name an export) are recomputed like every other fixture

references: the files outside the track directories that match each recorded pattern are recomputed with git grep at the pinned commit and must equal the list in the limit; an absence holds only while the same search finds nothing in its scope and the anchor search in that scope still finds exactly the recorded paths

documents: the per-file table, every "<n> tests" figure, the NESTED_SUITE line and the base commit in README.md describe the pinned base commit and are compared with this record, whose counts and first runner line the commands level reproduces
not_recomputed: ci_observations: read once from the CI API (gh api, read-only) and kept for traceability; no test re-reads them
environment: describes the machine this record was generated on

prose: limit statements, fixture origins, the title and this text are bound only by artifact_digest, which reports an edit that is not re-sealed; an editor who re-seals the record is caught only by review of the diff and by the recomputed values above
the files inside the installed packages (ajv and the packages it requires): not hashed; only their versions are compared with package-lock.json at the base commit

support data: the inputs of the fixtures are synthetic values written for this record plus the pinned fixture adapter package; none of them is the output of a real adapter or of a scan of a real repository, and their values are not independently checked
README.md: only the numbers and the base commit named above are recomputed, not the explanatory text
